feedback: Judged from earlier races only; this candidate has not raced. Its geometry and controller match iteration 7 and iteration 9 exactly (mass 0.5, body_length 0.12, wheel_track 0.12, kp 4.5, ki 0.02, kd 1.0, base_speed 1.1, five sensors at y 0.08 with x spread of ±0.05, sensor_size 0.016, line_loss last_direction). Those settings finished 60/60 trials in both iterations, scoring 929.76, the best raced score. Iteration 8 showed that base_speed 1.2 cost slalom finishes (18/20, score 908.2), so 1.1 is the safe speed ceiling. Iteration 10 showed that ki 0.10 scored 929.42, slightly below the verified design, so the integral change is reverted. The candidate is valid and is the best-supported design available. Another revision round would cost two action runs for a change with a few points of expected gain at most, and the verified design is the safer choice for an unseen final track. Nothing in the candidate is obviously broken. Line-loss events (about one per run, worth up to roughly 100 points) have not responded to any gain, sensor or speed change in iterations 3 to 10, so this race will not be used to chase them.
requested_changes: No change is requested because the candidate is approved unchanged. Read the race output in this order: completion and progress on all three tracks, then max_error and steering_oscillation on the slalom (iteration 7 values 0.0233 and 0.25) to confirm margin, then line_loss_events and rms_error for the record.
If a future race is run with this design, keep base_speed at 1.1, because iteration 8 showed that 1.2 lost slalom finishes, and keep ki at 0.02, because iteration 10 showed that ki 0.10 did not help.
Do not change the sensor layout or line_loss in any follow-up, because sensor y is already at its maximum of 0.08 and the single line-loss event per run has not moved under any tested change.
